name: Frugll
old_description: Frugll customers are able to save over 50% on their solar installs.
about:
Frugll was founded in 2017 in Salt Lake City, Utah, by co-founders Jordan Folsom and Josh Giddings. The company began with a mission to help homeowners maximize solar savings through a direct-to-consumer approach that eliminates sales commissions and marketing overhead.

The firm designs and installs residential photovoltaic systems, handling everything from initial consultation and system engineering to permitting, installation, and ongoing maintenance. Its proprietary software automates quoting and project management, allowing the team to pass cost savings directly to customers. To date, the company reports more than 1,500 completed installations and a network of over 190,000 installs, with an average customer savings of 52 percent compared with traditional installers.

Frugll serves individual homeowners across its service territories, focusing on the residential solar market. Its customers are typically property owners seeking to reduce electricity costs and achieve a faster return on investment, with payback periods cited between two and five years.

The company differentiates itself by removing sales commissions from the pricing structure, using custom automation to lower overhead, and including full-service maintenance for the life of the system. Leadership emphasizes a referral-driven culture and a commitment to educating customers about the economics of solar power.

name: Full Spectrum Solar
old_description: Full Spectrum Solar is a family owned and operated business that has been proudly serving Wisconsin for 20-years. Founded by brothers and UW-Madison Mechanical Engineering alumni, Burke and Mark have always strived to create a company culture that believes that the ethics of good business practice and contributing to the wellness of nature come first. We pride ourselves for how little we focus on marketing and instead believing that through great work and trust, our customers become our greatest supporters as a local small business.
about:
Full Spectrum Solar was founded in August 2002 in Madison, Wisconsin, by brothers Burke and Mark O'Neal, both University of Wisconsin–Madison mechanical engineering alumni. After Burke returned from a lead engineering role at a large California solar firm, the pair set out to build a Wisconsin-based solar contractor grounded in engineering rigor, quality installation, and long-term customer support. The company remains family-owned and operated.

The firm designs and installs solar photovoltaic systems, home battery backup, electric-vehicle charging stations, and heat-pump water heaters, and provides ongoing maintenance, repair, and storm-damage restoration for existing arrays. Its in-house team includes mechanical and electrical engineers, master and journeyman electricians, NABCEP-certified professionals, experienced roofers, and dedicated project managers. Since inception, Full Spectrum Solar has completed more than 1,500 installations totaling over 28 megawatts of capacity across southern Wisconsin, operating from offices in Madison and Waukesha.

Customers range from homeowners and farms to multifamily housing, healthcare facilities, recreation centers, offices, schools, public agencies, and nonprofit organizations. The portfolio includes ground-mounted arrays for agricultural operations, rooftop systems for commercial buildings, and community-scale projects for municipalities and nonprofits throughout the region.

The company distinguishes itself through an education-first approach—no commissioned salespeople—direct pricing, a single accountable project manager for each job, and a post-installation service department that remains available long after commissioning. Its Madison headquarters earned an ENERGY STAR 100/100 rating, and the firm emphasizes transparent communication, practical system recommendations, and standing behind its work for the life of the system.

name: Furniture Classics
old_description: Will be closing at 3:00 pm on Saturday, July 24th for seasonal maintenance.
about:
Furniture Classics operates from a 10,000-square-foot showroom at 433 West 5th Avenue in Anchorage, Alaska. The business traces its roots to the late 1950s when Anchorage pioneer Helen Calrquist opened Eckman's on 4th Avenue. After a bank takeover, she relocated to 5th Avenue. The store later became Nerland's Home Furnishings under the Nerland family, with longtime sales associate Erma Howell. In 1989, Howell partnered with current owner Colleen Hickey to establish Furniture Classics. The company is woman-owned.

As a furniture retailer and interior design studio, Furniture Classics offers a rotating inventory of American-made furniture, custom orders with over 2,000 fabric options, interior design services (many complimentary), white-glove delivery and installation across Anchorage and surrounding areas, and furniture assembly. The showroom spans 10,000 square feet and carries pieces in solid walnut, maple, cherry, leather, and velvet. Financing is available with 18 months deferred interest on purchases over $1,500.

The company serves residential customers throughout Alaska, including homeowners in Anchorage, Girdwood, Eagle River, and the Matanuska-Susitna Valley. Interior design clients range from individuals seeking full-room designs to those needing single-piece consultations. They also cater to customers looking for custom-made furniture and one-of-a-kind pieces sourced from national markets such as High Point.

Furniture Classics' stated mission is to provide quality American-made furniture to Alaskans at an affordable price without sacrificing comfort or style. The team emphasizes its 35-plus years of industry experience, which allows it to curate durable, high-quality brands and avoid lower-quality imitations. Designers help clients navigate thousands of fabric and style options to create functional, beautiful spaces.

name: Furniture Industries
old_description: As a third generation family business since 1952, we have grown to become one of the nation’s most respected ff&e providers to the design industry.
about:
Furniture Industries, based in Minneapolis, Minnesota, traces its roots to 1952 when it began as a furniture manufacturing and reupholstery operation. Now a third-generation family business, the company was shaped by Arnie Labofsky, who took the helm in the mid-1970s and instilled a culture of “do right by your clients and team members” that still guides the firm today.

The firm operates as a full-service FF&E (furniture, fixtures, and equipment) partner for the hospitality design industry. Its capabilities span interior design, procurement, project management, logistics, and installation. The team also offers prototypical design services for hotel brands and a “Ballpark Bids” program that delivers estimated budgets for up to 31 flags within days. Rather than manufacturing products, Furniture Industries coordinates sourcing from a network of brand partners to furnish new builds, renovations, and property improvement plans.

Clients include major hotel brands and developers such as IHG Hotels & Resorts (for which Furniture Industries is an approved purchasing agent), LivSmart Studios by Hilton, and Tru by Hilton. The company has executed projects for Douglas Carlson Development, Hotel Ventures Management, KM Hotels, Lighthouse Hospitality Group, Thomas Construction, Ehrhardt Properties, and Sonmar Management Corp., handling everything from 113-room hotel installations to large-scale renovations.

The company says its differentiation lies in “designing and procuring with purpose” — blending aesthetics, financial mindfulness, and schedule adherence. That philosophy, rooted in Labofsky’s original principle, aims to deliver spaces that captivate visually while respecting budget and timeline constraints.

name: Fusion EMS
old_description: Fusion specializes in turnkey and consigned EMS strategies, with a focus on high-mix, low-to-medium and high-volume production. We leverage deep expertise and a wide range of capabilities to develop custom solutions for our customers, and support your program every step of the way.
about:
Based in Hillsboro, Oregon, Fusion EMS has spent three decades providing electronics manufacturing services. The company focuses on turnkey and consigned EMS strategies, serving customers with high-mix, low-to-medium and high-volume production needs.

Fusion EMS offers a broad range of manufacturing capabilities, including PCB assembly, surface mount technology, conformal coating and potting, and test development. The company supports programs from new product introduction and quick-turn prototyping through box-build assembly, final packaging, and component purchasing with per-customer inventory management. Its processes emphasize robust engineering reviews, supplier input, and alternate component sourcing.

The company serves aerospace, medical and life sciences, industrial, and military and defense markets. Customers in these sectors rely on Fusion EMS for high-reliability electronic assemblies that meet stringent regulatory and quality requirements.

Fusion EMS differentiates itself by leveraging deep expertise and a wide range of capabilities to develop custom solutions, supporting customer programs at every step. All production personnel are trained and certified to IPC Class III standards, and the facility employs SPC and DMAIC principles to ensure product and process quality.

about:
G&R Industries was founded in 1992 in Goffstown, New Hampshire, through the merger of two established industry leaders. The company has since grown into a regional service provider for draft beer systems across New England.

The company specializes in routine beer line cleaning on a two-week cycle, draft system repairs, annual glycol chiller maintenance, and custom-designed beer system installations. Its technicians complete extensive internal training and operate marked, GPS-tracked vehicles to serve over 800 accounts, ranging from independent bars and restaurants to multi-location corporate clients.

G&R Industries serves bars, restaurants, event venues, and other hospitality businesses throughout New England. Its client base includes both corporate chains and independent operators, with a focus on the craft beer segment where knowledge of local trends and regulations is critical.

The company emphasizes trustworthiness built on decades of experience, reliable service backed by certified technicians and GPS-tracked vehicles, customer-centric flexibility with 24/7 support, and regional expertise in craft beer trends and regulations. Its stated mission is to make each client's beer system a worry-free, profit-driving asset.

name: G. B. Woodworking
old_description: GB Woodworking, founded in 1982, is the continuation of a lifelong passion for working with wood.
about:
G. B. Woodworking has operated from Boston, Massachusetts since 1982, when founder Gary Barcus turned a lifelong passion for woodworking into a full-time business. Barcus remains the sole owner and continues to oversee every project personally, from initial design through final installation.

The company produces custom cabinets, built-in bedroom and office furniture, bookcases, and architectural millwork for residential clients. Work begins with a complimentary design consultation, followed by shop fabrication using finishes such as precatalyzed lacquers, waterborne alkyd enamels, conversion varnishes, and catalyzed urethanes. Barcus emphasizes completing the majority of fabrication in the shop to keep on-site installation to one or two days for typical rooms, with larger installations taking up to a week.

Projects are concentrated in the Greater Boston area, including Brookline, Newton, Wellesley, Weston, and Pride’s Crossing. The firm frequently collaborates with interior designers and serves homeowners seeking high-end, fitted woodwork for renovations and new construction.

Barcus founded the business on the principle of client satisfaction above all, stating that he reads both the client and the drawings to anticipate issues before they arise. His hands-on involvement in design, shop work, and installation is presented as the primary differentiator, ensuring every piece receives his direct attention.
